statement: For Max-Cut (n≤1000, m≤20000) with incremental gain SA, restart budget allocation (depth vs breadth) does not affect score: 0.30s×3 restarts and 0.03s×30 restarts both achieve ~87.5 on the judge, indicating the solution landscape has many near-equivalent local optima reachable by either strategy.
regime: Max-Cut, n≤1000, m≤20000, 0.90s total budget, linear cooling SA with incremental gain
mechanism: Incremental gain tracking speeds SA iterations ~5x, but this does not raise the score ceiling because the quality bottleneck is not iteration count — it is the Max-Cut landscape structure. Random restarts (even shallow ones) reliably find optima near 87.5, so deeper per-restart exploration provides no additional benefit.
applicability_bounds: Applies to Max-Cut with the given size/density range. May not hold for larger graphs or sparser structures where deep exploration could find rarer, better optima.

statement: The ~87.5 score ceiling on Max-Cut (problem 192) is robust across SA configurations: geometric cooling (86.6), linear cooling (87.5), incremental gain + long SA (87.5), incremental gain + short SA (87.6). Further SA optimization is unlikely to push significantly beyond this ceiling.
regime: Max-Cut problem 192, judge evaluation, all SA variants tested across 3 iterations
mechanism: Multiple SA configurations with varying iteration speed, cooling schedules, and restart budgets all converge to ~87.5. This suggests the score is bounded by the problem structure (graph properties, checker scoring function) rather than algorithmic configuration. Breaking through would require a fundamentally different approach (e.g., problem-specific graph decomposition, semidefinite relaxation, or multi-flip neighborhoods).
applicability_bounds: Specific to problem 192 test cases and checker. Different test instances could have different ceilings.
